identification: Official Go source module for the Tailscale WireGuard mesh VPN client, daemon and CLI
decisive_evidence: All 841 archive members match the official v1.30.2 module; no substituted files.
v1.30.1 to v1.30.2 has nine changed files, zero added files and zero removed files. go.mod, go.sum and the entire DERP implementation are unchanged.

The flagged DERP client is byte-identical in v1.30.0, v1.30.1 and v1.30.2. v1.28.0 already has the same WebSocket debug option and selection logic; later DERP differences are netaddr-to-netip and typed atomic migrations.

The option is read through envknob.Bool, which defaults to false. In this release the WebSocket implementation is compiled on linux or js. JS uses WebSockets automatically; other supported builds require the option to parse as true.

connect selects the caller-supplied server URL or configured DERP-region node, dials with subprotocol derp, and passes the stream to derp.NewClient. magicsock uses it to relay WireGuard packets by peer public key.
New container-path probes only append a container annotation to host OS information. They do not suppress execution in analysis environments.
No added payload, obfuscation, command dispatch, credential theft or unauthorized transfer appears in the patch changes. Network relay behavior fits the VPN purpose.

obfuscation: Clear Go source; the relevant literal and call are directly represented in facts. No encoded execution path was found.
missing_context: No machine deployment, enrollment identity or operator authorization context supplied. VPN capabilities alone do not establish misuse.
trait_corrections: Move unchanged word matcher to micro-behaviors/os/env/provider::tailscale-derp-websocket-option, describe a reference rather than forced activation, set notable and remove unsupported ATT&CK/MBC mappings.

Remove the old source-identity exclusions: neutral configuration references should remain visible. Their only two exception composites are consequently unused and removed. The old copyright matcher omitted the year and did not recognize this source header.

Update both exact consumers; rename the BOF composite to bof-derp-websocket-mesh and remove unsupported forced/CDN claims from its description. Its conditions, hostile criticality, proximity, and scope are unchanged apart from the relocated reference.
Ancestor C2 selectors have JavaScript-only consumers, whereas the relocated atom never targets JavaScript; there is no lost coverage for those consumers.
